subject: The Newton-Raphson optimizer did not converge

messages.author: c4a3575d08613e47
messages.subject: The Newton-Raphson optimizer did not converge
parts:
Hello all

I'm trying to run a gaussian besag model in inla, but the program crashes after a second or so. Specifically, when I run this code

> require(INLA)
> 
> formula = KVMPris ~ f(location,model="besag",graph=W)
> model = inla(formula, family = "gaussian", data=data1)

(data and graph attached) Windows8 shows the standard Runtime error:
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Microsoft Visual C++ Runtime Library
---------------------------
Runtime Error!

Program: C:\Users\Demo\Documents\R\win-library\3.0\INLA\bin\windows\inla64.exe

This application has requested the Runtime to terminate it in an unusual way.
Please contact the application's support team for more information.
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

And inla prints this:

------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
GMRFLib version 3.0-0-snapshot, has recived error no [12]
Reason    : The Newton-Raphson optimizer did not converge
Message   : Condition `lambda < 1.0 / lambda_lim' is not TRUE
Function  : GMRFLib_init_GMRF_approximation_store__intern
File      : approx-inference.c
Line      : 2694
RCSId     : file: approx-inference.c  hgid: 15fa1e788b12  date: Fri Sep 20 09:14:11 2013 +0200
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

I understand that the NR-optimizer is a part of the Laplace approksimation step, but I have no clue what to do about it. In this discussion group specifying a prior on the intercept has been suggested, but it doesn't seem to work in this case. Now I have next to no experience with INLA, so it is entirely possible that the solution is very simple, in which case I apologize in advance :)

Regards,
Claus Vestergaard

messages.author: bbb9357156c132fe
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] The Newton-Raphson optimizer did not converge
parts:
Hi Claus,
As far as I can see, this is a scaling issue.  It runs fine with 
formula = (KVMPris)/1000 ~ f(location,model="besag",graph=W)

(It also works with a log-transform)

The default priors in INLA usually assume the data is O(1), otherwise they need to be re-scaled so everything is the same size.  

Håvard may be able to be more useful on how to actually re-scale the prior.

D

On 11 Nov 2013, at 10:45, Claus H. Vestergaard <claus.h.v...@gmail.com> wrote:

model = inla(formula, family = "gaussian", data=data1)

parts:
Hi Daniel,

I am new to INLA but run into the same problem Claus had. I am practising a space-time modelling using the code below
district_time_id = seq(1,nrow(my_neo))
GH.adj.path = "Ghana_D.graph"
#Formula
formula.spt = NMR/1000 ~  1+ f(OBJECTID,
                         model="bym",
                         graph=GH.adj.path,
                         hyper=list(prec.unstruct=list(prior="loggamma",param=c(1,0.01)), 
                                    prec.spatial=list(prior="loggamma",param=c(1,0.01)))) +
  f(yr.idx, model="iid",
    hyper=list(prec=list(prior="loggamma",param=c(1,0.01)))) +
  f(yr.idx2, model="rw1",
    hyper=list(prec=list(prior="loggamma",param=c(1,0.01)))) +
  f(district_time_id, model="iid",
    hyper=list(prec=list(prior="loggamma",param=c(1,0.01))))

#Run INLA
output3 = inla(formula.spt,
               family="gaussian",
               data=my_neo,
               offset=log(PM2.5),
               verbose=TRUE, keep = TRUE)
summary(output3)  

I got this error

GMRFLib version 3.0-0-snapshot, has recived error no [12]
Reason    : The Newton-Raphson optimizer did not converge
Message   : Condition `lambda < 1.0 / lambda_lim' is not TRUE
Function  : GMRFLib_init_GMRF_approximation_store__intern
File      : approx-inference.c

Line      : 2947
RCSId     : file: approx-inference.c  hgid: 0bed76828f01  date: Tue Sep 03 11:21:49 2019 +0300

Thank you
